personas.title: Interactive human operator
goals: Type, paste, select, scroll, resize, zoom, and navigate without noticeable lag or lost intent.
Understand overload and recovery without needing internal architecture knowledge.
success_outcomes: Native input reaches the intended pane and a coherent frame is presented within the declared journey SLOs.
Text, focus, selection, cursor, geometry, and policy feedback remain readable and correct through recovery.

personas.title: Meta-agent fleet operator
goals: Supervise agents through Robot, MCP, mission, transaction, approval, search, and fleet-state surfaces.
Receive bounded machine-readable results with exact pane, mux, policy, and candidate identity.
success_outcomes: Calls remain bounded, idempotent where required, and explicit about refusal, uncertainty, and partial failure.
The operator can explain fleet state and take a safe next action without scraping ambiguous GUI text.

personas.title: Unattended automation agent
goals: Execute approved workflows, typed waits, and bounded pane actions without human timing assumptions.
Recover deterministically from cancellation, rate limits, approvals, disconnects, and partial failure.
success_outcomes: Mutations are replay-safe, policy-gated, and accompanied by durable receipts.
Absent authority or capability produces an explicit refusal rather than an unsafe or silent fallback.

personas.title: Incident responder
goals: Diagnose lag, failure, gaps, resource pressure, and failed recovery with bounded privacy-safe evidence.
Reproduce the relevant candidate and topology state and identify a safe next action.
success_outcomes: Evidence distinguishes measurements, proxies, missing data, candidate identity, and causal uncertainty.
The responder can hand off a redacted portable bundle without creating a second transcript store.

fleet_points.title: Two-pane product floor
workload_characteristics: Interactive typing, approval, pane switching, capture, and restart regression floor.

fleet_points.title: Normal daily project
workload_characteristics: Normal coding, approvals, search, capture, and routine pane churn.
Mixed interactive and background activity with bounded maintenance.

fleet_points.title: Loaded protected-interaction fleet
workload_characteristics: Burst output, maintenance, policy activity, indexing, and protected interactive work.
Fairness and overload behavior must remain visible and bounded.

fleet_points.title: Target-class mission
workload_characteristics: Explicit resource, fairness, recovery, and long-session qualification.
Four-hour and 24-hour runs plus selected 72-hour evidence on the declared target class.

topologies.title: Local Mac mux
topologies.description: The GUI, mux authority, panes, and primary applications execute on the same Mac; loopback IPC is allowed and unrelated remote build work does not change this topology.

topologies.title: Mac client to LAN remote mux
topologies.description: The local Mac owns the interactive GUI and client while the authoritative mux and application path crosses the named LAN route to trj; route, transport, endpoint, mux generation, RTT, jitter, loss, disconnects, and reconnects are explicit evidence.

target_classes.title: Local Apple M4 Pro native target
target_classes.hardware_identity: Mac16,11 M4 Pro; every run must retain the exact SKU, memory, OS, display, renderer, thermal, and power identity.

target_classes.title: Base Apple M5 native target
target_classes.hardware_identity: Base Apple M5 target identity; every run must retain the exact SKU, memory, OS, display, renderer, thermal, and power identity, and no result may be inferred from M4.

target_classes.title: Transitional Apple M5 Pro/Max planning row
target_classes.hardware_identity: Transitional schema-v1 planning identity only. Every lane is permanently frozen at unknown/missing/not_run/unknown and cannot retain candidate, route, evidence, or blocker references. Separate M5 Pro and M5 Max classes under ft-interactive-swarm-product-convergence-7xqz4.12.3.1 are required before either SKU can carry qualification authority.

target_classes.title: trj Threadripper PRO 5995WX native target
target_classes.hardware_identity: Named trj host with AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5995WX and 128 hardware threads; every run must retain CPU topology, SMT, affinity, memory, kernel, thermal, power, and route identity.

actor_modes.title: Native interactive human
actor_modes.description: A person drives native AppKit input and judges presented frames, focus, text, policy feedback, and recovery.

actor_modes.title: Supervised meta-agent
actor_modes.description: A machine operator supervises agents through bounded Robot, MCP, mission, transaction, approval, search, and fleet-state calls.

actor_modes.title: Unattended automation
actor_modes.description: An approved workflow acts and waits without human timing assumptions while preserving cancellation, policy, and replay safety.

actor_modes.title: Privacy-safe incident response
actor_modes.description: A human or automated responder gathers bounded diagnostics, forms falsifiable causal candidates, replays evidence, and selects a safe next action.

gates.title: Catalog identity and exact coverage binding
gates.description: The persona, actor mode, exact pane count, topology, target, claim, producer, and artifact identities must resolve without implicit ranges or adjacent-cell inference.

gates.title: Exact installed candidate identity
gates.description: GUI, mux server, CLI, source, build, protocol, config, renderer, display, route, and application identity must be exact and fresh before a result is admissible.

gates.title: Native input-to-present interaction
gates.description: Native event receipt, mux and PTY delivery, application response, render invalidation, draw completion, and presentation must be correlated; a proxy slice cannot qualify the full path.

gates.title: Resize, zoom, reflow, and visual quality
gates.description: Continuous resize, storms, zoom, DPI changes, display migration, intermediate frames, final authoritative geometry, Unicode, images, cursor, selection, and glyph-cache states must satisfy deterministic and declared human-review checks.

gates.title: Remote route, transport, and mux identity
gates.description: A remote run must identify the LAN, Wi-Fi, or tailnet route, endpoint, mux generation, RTT, jitter, loss, disconnects, reconnects, and resynchronization; distributed observation is not a remote-mux substitute.

gates.title: Fleet fairness and protected interaction
gates.description: Exact fleet points must retain a protected interactive pane under burst output, background work, approvals, capture, indexing, and maintenance without starvation or unbounded queues.

gates.title: Long-session resource and stability envelope
gates.description: Four-hour, 24-hour, and selected 72-hour runs must bound memory, CPU, queues, file descriptors, storage growth, compaction, thermals, and degradation on an admissible target.

gates.title: Robot, MCP, workflow, and policy correctness
gates.description: Machine calls and workflows must be bounded, cancel-correct, idempotent where required, policy-gated, receipt-bearing, and explicit when authority or capability is absent.

gates.title: Failure, rollback, recovery, and convergence
gates.description: Disconnect, crash, stale candidate, failed update, overload, and restart paths must preserve exact final intent or disclose loss, converge without duplicate mutation, and retain bounded recovery evidence.

gates.title: Keyboard, VoiceOver, reduced-motion, and low-vision equivalence
gates.description: Applicable journeys must preserve keyboard-only operation, stable focus, VoiceOver semantics and geometry, reduced-motion behavior, low-vision readability, IME input, and equivalent recovery feedback.

gates.title: Privacy-safe diagnostic and evidence contract
gates.description: Artifacts must default to redacted identities, measurements, hashes, gaps, confidence, and falsifiers; content-bearing capture requires explicit authority, scope, retention, and expiry.

gates.title: Native target-class qualification
gates.description: M4 Pro, M5, M5 Pro or Max, and trj results remain target-specific; unavailable targets and skipped target-class evidence cannot be inferred from another architecture or host.

gates.title: Unified fail-closed release promotion
gates.description: Promotion requires an exact direct producer, admissible native evidence, a passing run, satisfied gates, human authority where required, and derived claim updates; absence, proxy evidence, or stale identity fails closed.

journey_definitions.title: Clean Mac first hour
setup: Record package, app, CLI, mux, config, renderer, display, OS, target, and first-run authority identity.
Begin from a declared clean compatible Mac and install the packaged, signed candidate.
steady_work: Launch, complete setup, open a project, start two useful agents, type, paste, switch panes, search, approve, resize, and zoom.
Quit and relaunch through the supported product path without manual source-tree substitution.
failure_overload: Exercise missing config, denied authority, stale companion, and interrupted first launch with typed and actionable feedback.
recovery: Resume or retry idempotently, preserve accepted setup choices, and reach the same authoritative candidate without duplicate side effects.
teardown: Exit cleanly, preserve the declared session state, and emit a privacy-safe setup and relaunch outcome record.
user_outcomes: A new operator reaches useful two-agent work and a successful relaunch within the declared first-hour envelope.
No manual hidden prerequisite, stale binary, or ambiguous authority is required.
accessibility_expectations: The entire setup, launch, project, pane, and relaunch path is keyboard operable with visible focus and useful VoiceOver names.
Zoom, contrast, reduced motion, and error feedback remain usable without pointer-only or color-only cues.
privacy_expectations: Setup evidence excludes secrets, raw terminal content, credentials, and private paths by default.
Any diagnostics record only redacted identities, durations, decisions, and reason codes.
evidence_requirements: Retain signed package and running-component identity, setup timing, interaction spans, final screenshots or declared visual review, relaunch result, gaps, and artifact hashes.
Mark manual steps, skipped checks, unavailable targets, and human review explicitly.

journey_definitions.title: Two-agent everyday project for four hours
setup: Record pane, mux, application, route, display, renderer, config, and target identities.
Start the exact packaged candidate with two real project agents in the selected local or Mac-to-LAN topology.
steady_work: Perform four hours of typing, paste, search, approval, pane navigation, scrollback, resize, zoom, and agent supervision.
Include quiet, normal, and burst-output phases while preserving a protected interactive pane.
failure_overload: Inject rate limits, burst output, one agent restart, and a bounded transport interruption when the topology is remote.
recovery: Recover exact pane intent, focus, geometry, search state, and pending approvals without duplicate input or hidden local fallback.
teardown: Stop the agents and product cleanly, verify durable receipts and explicit gaps, and retain bounded four-hour evidence.
user_outcomes: Everyday two-agent work remains responsive, legible, predictable, and recoverable for four hours.
The final state matches accepted user and agent intent.
accessibility_expectations: Keyboard traversal, focus, VoiceOver state, reduced-motion feedback, IME, and low-vision zoom remain equivalent through the session.
Recovery does not require pointer-only action.
privacy_expectations: Latency and resource evidence uses redacted correlation identifiers rather than key or pane contents.
Any content-bearing sample has explicit authority, scope, retention, and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain native input-to-present spans, route measurements when remote, frame and resize quality, resource trends, queue ages, recovery result, gaps, hashes, and replay instructions.
Distinguish direct measurements from proxies and record instrumentation overhead.

journey_definitions.title: Twenty-pane normal daily swarm
setup: Pin candidate, mux, route, storage, index, policy, renderer, display, and target identity.
Create exactly twenty panes with declared real-agent, shell, and workload roles in the selected topology.
steady_work: Run normal coding, approvals, search, capture, pane churn, scrollback, resize, zoom, Robot or MCP queries, and bounded background maintenance.
Preserve a designated interactive pane and observable agent state transitions.
failure_overload: Apply synchronized output bursts, pane churn, index or capture pressure, approvals, and a recoverable agent or connection failure.
recovery: Restore authoritative pane state, interaction priority, machine envelopes, search freshness, and exact pending intent within declared bounds.
teardown: Drain bounded work, stop the fleet, verify durable state and explicit gaps, and archive the exact q020 manifest and outcome.
user_outcomes: A normal twenty-pane day remains responsive for the human and bounded for machine operators.
Background work cannot silently starve input, presentation, policy, or recovery.
accessibility_expectations: Keyboard and VoiceOver navigation expose twenty-pane identity, ordering, state, focus, and alerts without excessive announcement churn.
Reduced-motion and low-vision modes preserve actionable overload and recovery feedback.
privacy_expectations: Fleet evidence retains typed event classes, counts, timings, hashes, and redaction receipts instead of pane transcripts.
Search and incident samples follow declared content authority and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain the exact twenty-pane manifest, native interaction spans, Robot or MCP call bounds, queue and fairness metrics, frame quality, resource trends, recovery convergence, gaps, and artifact hashes.
Record every skipped or unavailable phase and the effect of instrumentation.

journey_definitions.title: Fifty-pane Mac-to-trj loaded fleet
setup: Declare a protected interactive pane and record both host identities, CPU topology, route, protocol, mux generation, renderer, display, storage, and workload.
Create exactly fifty panes on the authoritative trj mux and connect from the exact Mac candidate over the named LAN route.
steady_work: Run loaded agent output, capture, search, policy, approval, indexing, maintenance, resize, zoom, scrolling, and machine supervision.
Continuously exercise the protected pane while measuring native input-to-present and remote round-trip segments.
failure_overload: Drive burst output, maintenance collision, queue pressure, route jitter, loss, and a bounded disconnect while preserving diagnostic observability.
recovery: Reconnect and resynchronize to the exact mux generation, preserve or explicitly reject pending input, and converge text, geometry, search, policy, and agent state.
teardown: Drain or cancel bounded work, stop the fifty-pane fleet, and retain manifests, route evidence, fairness evidence, gaps, and final convergence.
user_outcomes: The protected pane remains responsive and visually coherent while fifty remote panes produce realistic load.
Overload degrades explicitly and recovery never duplicates or silently loses user intent.
accessibility_expectations: Keyboard and VoiceOver access to the protected pane, fleet status, overload alerts, reconnection, and recovery remains practical at fifty panes.
Resize, zoom, reduced motion, contrast, and focus remain readable under remote load.
privacy_expectations: Remote evidence includes route, timing, counts, hashes, reason codes, and redaction receipts without raw pane or key content.
Cross-host bundles use explicit retention and access authority.
evidence_requirements: Retain exact Mac and trj identities, fifty-pane manifest, route telemetry, native and remote latency segments, fairness, frames, resources, queue bounds, disconnect and recovery results, gaps, hashes, and replay commands.
Separate direct route and presentation measurements from load-generator or headless proxies.

journey_definitions.title: Two-hundred-pane target-class mission
setup: Preflight resource headroom, artifact retention, privacy tier, recovery checkpoints, and duration authority.

Create exactly two hundred declared panes on the selected target topology with a protected interactive pane and exact candidate, host, route, CPU, memory, storage, renderer, display, policy, and workload identity.
steady_work: Run the target mission for four hours and 24 hours, plus the selected 72-hour scenario, with realistic agents, bursts, approvals, search, capture, indexing, backups, GC, WAL, rules, resize, zoom, and supervision.
Measure protected interaction, fairness, presentation quality, bounded machine calls, resource slopes, and thermal or affinity state.
failure_overload: Exercise declared saturation, synchronized output, maintenance collision, route disruption when remote, component restart, storage pressure, and thermal or scheduler variance without hiding degraded intervals.
recovery: Shed or defer work by declared policy, reconnect or restart safely, converge the exact two-hundred-pane state, and prove no duplicate mutation, unbounded backlog, or silent gap.
teardown: Quiesce the mission, verify durable and final user intent, release resources, and seal the exact duration and target artifact bundle.
user_outcomes: A q200 mission remains operable, explainable, bounded, and recoverable on the declared target for the declared duration.
No result is generalized to more than two hundred panes, another fleet point, another host, or another architecture.
accessibility_expectations: Protected interaction, fleet navigation, alerts, approvals, and recovery remain keyboard and VoiceOver accessible without unbounded notification load.
Reduced-motion and low-vision presentation remain legible through overload, display changes, and recovery.
privacy_expectations: Long-run artifacts retain aggregate and redacted measurements, hashes, resource and route identities, reason codes, and gaps rather than terminal transcripts.
Content samples require narrow explicit authority, access control, retention, and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain exact q200 and target manifests, four-hour, 24-hour, and selected 72-hour identities, native latency, remote segments, fairness, frame quality, resource slopes, thermals, queues, failures, recovery, explicit gaps, overhead, hashes, and replay instructions.
A skipped target-class run remains skipped_not_proven and cannot support a resource or 200-plus claim.

journey_definitions.title: Rate-limit, compaction, approval, Verified Submit, deduplication, and attention day
setup: Bind every mutation and prompt to a stable correlation and idempotency identity.
Create declared agent, policy, approval, mission, transaction, rate-limit, and attention states with exact pane and candidate identity.
steady_work: Supervise mixed agent work through Robot and MCP surfaces, approvals, compaction, deduplicated attention, policy feedback, and Verified Submit.
Keep human and machine views consistent while bounded waits and actions proceed.
failure_overload: Generate rate limits, duplicate notifications, stale approvals, conflicting submissions, cancellation, slow consumers, and denied authority.
recovery: Deduplicate safely, preserve causal order, expire stale authority, resume approved work, and expose every refusal or unresolved ambiguity.
teardown: Drain or cancel pending work, close approvals and transactions, and retain durable receipts and the final attention state.
user_outcomes: The operator sees one actionable representation of each real need and can submit or refuse exactly once.
Automation neither spins nor guesses when policy, authority, rate limit, or capability blocks progress.
accessibility_expectations: Attention, approval, denial, rate-limit, and recovery state is available through keyboard and assistive semantics without color-only or animation-only meaning.
Focus and announcement order remain stable under deduplication.
privacy_expectations: Receipts retain decisions, identities, hashes, reason codes, and timing without raw prompt or pane content.
Verified Submit evidence records authority and result without retaining secrets.
evidence_requirements: Retain bounded-call timings, queue ages, deduplication decisions, policy and approval receipts, idempotency outcomes, cancellation, final attention state, gaps, and hashes.
Show that simulated, fixture, and real-agent evidence are labeled separately.

journey_definitions.title: Concurrent search, index, backup, GC, WAL, rules, and incident maintenance day
setup: Set bounded maintenance budgets and identify protected interaction and machine-control work.
Prepare declared capture, search, index, storage, backup, GC, WAL, rules, incident, and fleet state on the exact candidate.
steady_work: Run foreground typing, search, approval, capture, and agent supervision while search, indexing, backup, GC, WAL, rules, and incident tasks overlap.
Observe scheduling, queueing, cancellation, storage, and freshness without serializing away realistic contention.
failure_overload: Apply storage pressure, index backlog, long readers, rule bursts, backup collision, cancelled tasks, and slow consumers.
recovery: Bound, defer, or cancel background work, restore freshness and storage invariants, and return protected foreground work to the declared envelope.
teardown: Drain maintenance safely, verify WAL, backup, index, capture, and incident consistency, and retain final resource and queue state.
user_outcomes: Routine maintenance cannot make the terminal feel hung or make machine control unbounded.
Degradation, freshness, deferred work, and recovery remain explicit and actionable.
accessibility_expectations: Maintenance pressure and recovery feedback remains keyboard reachable and assistive-technology readable without announcement storms.
Foreground focus and low-vision presentation remain stable during background churn.
privacy_expectations: Maintenance evidence uses counts, sizes, durations, hashes, state transitions, and redaction receipts rather than indexed content.
Backup and incident artifacts declare access, retention, and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain foreground latency, bounded-call results, maintenance queue ages, storage and WAL state, index freshness, resource trends, cancellations, recovery, gaps, hashes, and overhead.
Record whether workload components were real, replayed, simulated, or unavailable.

journey_definitions.title: Remote host unavailable at launch and later returns
setup: Record route, endpoint, expected mux generation, pending intent, policy, and retry budget.
Select the exact Mac-to-LAN remote topology and candidate while the named authoritative remote host is unavailable.
steady_work: Launch and observe bounded unavailable-state behavior through native, Robot, MCP, workflow, and incident surfaces as applicable.
Keep local UI and machine APIs responsive while no remote authority exists.
failure_overload: Maintain unavailability through retries, route changes, stale discovery, queued actions, and concurrent local activity.
recovery: Return the remote host, re-authenticate or reconnect, bind the authoritative mux generation, reconcile pending actions, and resynchronize without duplicate input.
teardown: Close or retain the recovered session by explicit choice and archive unavailable, retry, reconnect, reconciliation, and final-state evidence.
user_outcomes: Unavailable remote authority is explicit, bounded, and non-blocking for the local product.
Recovery reaches exact final intent without silently substituting a local mux or stale remote generation.
accessibility_expectations: Unavailable, retry, route, reconnect, and recovered states have stable keyboard focus and useful VoiceOver announcements.
Progress and failure do not rely only on animation or color.
privacy_expectations: Route and reconnect evidence redacts endpoints and private paths while retaining stable correlation and transport identity.
Queued action contents are excluded by default.
evidence_requirements: Retain candidate and endpoint identity, route state, bounded retry timings, queued-action counts, local responsiveness, reconnect spans, mux-generation reconciliation, duplicate-prevention result, gaps, and hashes.
Record any local-only run as a separate cell, never as remote fallback proof.

journey_definitions.title: LAN, Wi-Fi, tailnet roam plus sleep and wake
setup: Declare the allowed LAN, Wi-Fi, and tailnet transitions plus sleep and wake sequence.
Connect the exact Mac client to the named remote mux and record initial LAN route, endpoint, mux generation, pending intent, display, renderer, and target identity.
steady_work: Type, supervise agents, search, scroll, resize, and zoom while transitioning among declared routes and display states.
Maintain typed connection and route state across background and foreground changes.
failure_overload: Exercise packet loss, jitter, route disappearance, sleep, wake, stale sockets, simultaneous output, and input near each transition.
recovery: Reconnect on the intended route, bind the exact mux generation, resynchronize text and geometry, and resolve pending input without duplication or reordering.
teardown: Return to the declared final route or disconnect explicitly and retain transition, resynchronization, presentation, and final-intent evidence.
user_outcomes: The session remains understandable during mobility and returns to exact final intent after each route or power transition.
The product never presents stale connectivity as healthy.
accessibility_expectations: Connection, route, sleep, wake, and resynchronization changes are keyboard discoverable and announced without excessive repetition.
Focus, zoom, contrast, reduced motion, and display geometry remain usable after wake.
privacy_expectations: Network evidence retains route class and redacted endpoint identity rather than raw addresses, keys, or pane content.
Sleep and wake artifacts use bounded retention.
evidence_requirements: Retain route timeline, RTT, jitter, loss, socket and mux generation, native interaction spans, pending-input reconciliation, frame and geometry convergence, gaps, overhead, hashes, and replay steps.
Differentiate direct LAN, Wi-Fi, and tailnet results.

journey_definitions.title: Live component update, watcher handoff, candidate failure, and rollback
setup: Record all component, protocol, config, bundle, and rollback identities.
Start a healthy exact candidate with active panes, watcher, GUI, mux, storage, machine clients, and a declared update candidate.
steady_work: Continue interactive and machine work while staging and initiating the supported component update and watcher handoff.
Expose current and candidate identity throughout the transition.
failure_overload: Fail the candidate at declared preflight, handoff, launch, protocol, health, or migration boundaries while foreground work continues.
recovery: Rollback or complete the update atomically, restore one authoritative watcher and mux path, reconcile queued work, and prevent mixed-version claims.
teardown: Verify the final installed and running identities, stop obsolete components safely, and retain update, failure, rollback, and continuity receipts.
user_outcomes: The operator always knows which candidate is authoritative and can continue or recover without hidden mixed-version state.
Failed updates do not lose panes, duplicate actions, or strand machine clients.
accessibility_expectations: Update, handoff, failure, rollback, and final identity are keyboard operable and announced with stable focus.
Progress and authority do not depend only on animation or color.
privacy_expectations: Update evidence retains component hashes, decisions, timings, health, and reason codes without terminal or credential content.
Rollback bundles use bounded access and retention.
evidence_requirements: Retain old and new candidate hashes, component graph, handoff spans, health decisions, queued-work reconciliation, final authority, continuity, gaps, and replay instructions.
Any manual recovery or human authority remains explicit.

journey_definitions.title: Crash and recover GUI, watcher, mux, renderer, storage, and connections
setup: Create bounded checkpoints and declare each component crash injection.
Start the exact candidate with declared active pane, storage, search, policy, renderer, watcher, connection, and machine-client state.
steady_work: Maintain interactive and machine work while observing component health, durable receipts, frame state, queues, and resource bounds.
Capture the authoritative pre-crash state without raw content by default.
failure_overload: Crash GUI, watcher, mux, renderer, storage, and connection components separately and in declared compound cases.
recovery: Restart the correct component, reject stale generations, restore durable state, reconcile pending work, redraw coherently, and disclose every gap or lost capability.
teardown: Verify final component identity, pane and machine state, storage consistency, connections, presentation, and resource cleanup before sealing evidence.
user_outcomes: A component crash has a bounded, understandable recovery path and does not silently corrupt or duplicate work.
The recovered product presents authoritative text, geometry, focus, and policy state.
accessibility_expectations: Crash and recovery feedback, relaunch, focus restoration, and error actions remain keyboard and assistive-technology usable.
Recovered focus and announcements avoid disorientation and repeated alert storms.
privacy_expectations: Crash evidence defaults to hashes, component state, backtrace classifications, timings, counts, gaps, and redaction receipts.
Memory or pane-content collection requires explicit narrow authority and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain component identity, injection point, health timeline, durable receipts, pending-work reconciliation, storage checks, presentation convergence, resource cleanup, gaps, hashes, and replay instructions.
Distinguish successful restart from complete end-to-end recovery.

journey_definitions.title: Keyboard-only, VoiceOver, reduced-motion, and low-vision operator day
setup: Record assistive technology, OS, app, renderer, display, target, and scenario identity.
Start the exact native candidate with the declared accessibility corpus, keyboard configuration, VoiceOver, reduced-motion, low-vision, IME, display, and zoom settings.
steady_work: Complete project, tab, split, pane, command palette, dialog, approval, search, scroll, resize, zoom, display migration, IME, and recovery tasks without pointer dependence.
Exercise names, roles, values, ordering, announcements, geometry, focus, contrast, cursor, selection, and policy feedback.
failure_overload: Apply output bursts, alert churn, resize storms, connection loss, denied policy, and component recovery while assistive features remain active.
recovery: Restore a stable logical focus, correct VoiceOver geometry and ordering, readable final presentation, and equivalent recovery actions without pointer-only steps.
teardown: Return settings and focus safely, record human-locked observations where required, and retain redacted deterministic and review artifacts.
user_outcomes: A keyboard, VoiceOver, reduced-motion, or low-vision operator can complete and recover the same supported work with comparable authority and clarity.
No machine replay fabricates a human accessibility judgment.
accessibility_expectations: All corpus requirements for names, roles, values, ordering, announcements, geometry, focus, keyboard traversal, reduced motion, zoom, contrast, IME, and feedback apply.
Critical intermediate and final states must both remain understandable.
privacy_expectations: Accessibility evidence excludes spoken or terminal content by default and retains scenario IDs, semantic properties, geometry, timings, decisions, and review locks.
Any recording requires explicit consent, scope, access, retention, and expiry.
evidence_requirements: Retain exact scenario and target identity, semantic tree assertions, keyboard traces without key contents, geometry, focus, announcements by classification, resize and zoom frames, recovery, human-review records, gaps, and hashes.
Separate deterministic checks from human-locked judgments.

journey_definitions.title: Field lag report through privacy-safe diagnosis and replay
setup: State candidate causes, confidence, falsifiers, and missing measurements before collection.
Start from a real lag report and bind the exact candidate, target, topology, route, pane class, renderer, display, workload, time window, privacy authority, and evidence budget.
steady_work: Collect bounded native input, mux, PTY, application, transport, render, presentation, queue, resource, and workload signals while preserving operator usability.
Correlate measurements without retaining raw key or pane content by default.
failure_overload: Exercise unavailable probes, sampling overhead, gaps, clock uncertainty, stale identity, collection failure, and contradictory signals.
recovery: Reduce collection safely, seal a redacted portable bundle, replay the admissible portions on the named target, update causal candidates, and identify a safe next action.
teardown: Expire temporary authority, remove transient collection state by the supported retention path, and retain hashes, receipts, uncertainty, and handoff status.
user_outcomes: A responder can distinguish network, mux, application, rendering, presentation, resource, and instrumentation causes without guessing.
The affected operator receives an actionable mitigation or an honest missing-evidence result.
accessibility_expectations: Incident collection, consent, status, stop, export, and mitigation actions remain keyboard and assistive-technology operable.
Diagnostic overlays do not obscure focus, text, alerts, or reduced-motion expectations.
privacy_expectations: Bundles default to redacted correlations, durations, counts, hashes, classifications, identities, gaps, confidence, and falsifiers.
Content-bearing data requires explicit authority, scope, redaction tier, access, retention, expiry, and audit receipt.
evidence_requirements: Retain exact candidate and target identity, direct versus proxy measurements, unavailable probes, overhead, gaps, clocks, route, resource and latency signals, causal candidates, confidence, falsifiers, hashes, and replay commands.
Cross-machine replay must state which observations are reproduced and which remain field-only.

journey_definitions.title: Version-pinned Codex, Claude, Gemini, and supported-agent dogfood
setup: Separate real-agent runs from simulated or replayed fixtures.
Pin the exact FrankenTerm candidate, supported agent products and versions, model or profile identity, authentication posture, policy, project fixture, pane manifest, topology, and target.
steady_work: Run representative coding, review, tool use, approval, search, compaction, rate limit, cancellation, pane navigation, Robot or MCP supervision, resize, and zoom workflows.
Observe human and machine outcomes without assuming equivalent behavior among agent products.
failure_overload: Exercise agent rate limits, compaction, prompts, tool denial, malformed or delayed output, restart, network interruption, and version drift.
recovery: Detect exact agent state, preserve policy and pending intent, resume or refuse safely, and avoid duplicate submissions or cross-agent inference.
teardown: Stop agents, revoke transient authority, retain version and outcome receipts, and separate content-free diagnostics from any explicitly authorized samples.
user_outcomes: Supported agent versions complete representative work with responsive human interaction and bounded machine supervision.
Compatibility claims name the exact agent, version, topology, fleet point, target, and evidence.
accessibility_expectations: Agent prompts, approvals, status, errors, and recovery actions remain keyboard and assistive-technology accessible.
High-volume agent output does not destroy focus, reduced-motion, zoom, contrast, or announcement usability.
privacy_expectations: Evidence excludes credentials, prompts, private code, and raw conversations by default while retaining versions, event classes, timings, hashes, and policy receipts.
Authorized samples have explicit redaction, access, retention, and expiry.

legacy_mappings.notes: Legacy operator-acceptance scenarios are reusable substrates only. Their stale local fallback wording does not satisfy fail-closed remote proof and they do not bind the exact 32 product cells.
Demo scenarios provide onboarding and deterministic regression material; a demo pass is not an exact native journey or support verdict.
The campaign's one-pane slice remains a diagnostic baseline. Product qualification starts at exact q002, and negative evidence narrows rather than promotes claims.
High-scale rehearsal and simulation artifacts can supply workload components, but simulated scale cannot qualify native interaction, target resources, or recovery.

readme_mappings.notes: The README 200-plus headline exceeds the catalog's exact q200 point. No open-ended above-200 support claim is permitted until a distinct producer and passing journey exist.

readme_mappings.notes: Capture can emit explicit gaps when continuity is not guaranteed. The catalog does not inherit an unconditional every-byte claim.
README capacity bands overlap at 200 and are not qualification points. This catalog uses exact q002, q020, q050, and q200 cells.

It identified and corrected forgeable v1 authority shape, revision-history, evidence-identity, transitional M5 Pro/Max, and lifecycle materialization gaps. change_history.summary: Initial contract-only catalog with four product personas, four exact fleet points, two mux topologies, four neutral target identities, four actor modes, thirteen fail-closed gates, fourteen field journeys, thirty-two required cells, exact and partial producer bindings, three target qualifications per cell, content-bound README mappings, and eight open contradictions.

Fail-closed authority hardening: retained append-only review and change revisions, rejected unsigned human dispositions in schema v1, required candidate and route identity for evidence, froze the transitional combined M5 Pro/Max lane, and enforced setup index zero as the pre-mutation identity/preflight boundary.
